fieldData.job-spec:
RDX Works created the technology behind the Radix Public Network and continues to aggressively develop that technology to ensure the network’s success. Going further, we wish to contribute to the network and its community by studying, developing, and proposing concepts for mature, long-term blockchain governance for that decentralized, public network. That’s where you come in.

Blockchain governance is an exciting new frontier. It is now a proven fact that blockchain-based networks can carry many billions of dollars of assets, as well as “decentralized finance” applications that bring those assets to life in functional financial systems that are used every day. This makes these networks a new kind of digital commonwealth – created, operated, and used by an open community of global users. Blockchain governance should answer the question “how will decisions about the present and future of these digital commonwealths be made?”

‍

What is governance?

Governance is so much more than just voting on a blockchain or ledger. It’s ensuring that all members that contribute to and rely on the technology not only have a way to propose changes and updates but also have a means of constructive debate and decision making, whilst also ensuring that decisions are not bogged down in bureaucracy.

If this sounds a lot like a national government - that is because a blockchain network could well be considered a kind of digital state – with the added challenges of being multi-jurisdictional, often populated by anonymous participants, supported by a wide range of stakeholders, and intimately tied into highly technical network mechanisms.


The Job

The above is why we are looking for a Governance Lead to work with the RDX Works leadership team, legal advisors, and community to develop and propose to the Radix community a governance system for the Radix network that is as resilient as a sovereign nation, and stands the test of time in an evolving decentralized world.

This is a truly unique opportunity (and not in the way that all other job descriptions say). What other job will allow you to help envision a completely new system of governance drawing on politics, philosophy, history, and new technology advances – and support a community in potentially implementing it?

We don’t want to copy existing blockchain governance, which overall hasn’t been very successful in creating the kind of inclusiveness, efficiency, and long-term resilience that we believe the Radix network needs to fulfil its mission. We want you to treat this as a blank canvas and think about the challenges facing governance of open, decentralized networks afresh.

Because this role is so unique, there is no one background that is the right fit. We care primarily about how you think, where you draw inspiration from and how you solve problems. No specific background is necessarily the right one - whether it be political science, systems engineering, law, philosophy, sociology, or something else entirely.

That is why for this recruitment process we’re doing something a bit different. Rather than limiting your application to telling us about your education and experience - we want you to solve a challenge as the first stage of the recruitment process.

We know that asking you to complete a challenge or task upfront is a lot to ask in this job market, so we are going to keep it as lightweight as possible and not ask you to do free work that we can use. We also hope you see this as an opportunity to test your thinking and fit for the role – and also have some fun!


The Challenge

A plane has crashed on a deserted island in the middle of the ocean, and you are one of the survivors.  There is no immediate hope of rescue – the survivors must assume that they and their children will live out their lives on the island with no hope of escape.

The 461 survivors consist of:

  • 1 pilot and 1 co-pilot
  • 9 crew members
  • 450 passengers

Assume that the island has fresh running water, fruits growing on trees and limited wild game and small wildlife and that the plane is beyond repair.

What system of governance might you propose to the group of survivors to ensure a functioning, long-term society of survivors that  work together for the shared goals of:

  • Best utilising the limited resources left from the plane and available on the island to survive
  • Dividing up responsibilities for work that must be done
  • Ensure that all survivors are encouraged and enabled to participate in the process


Your Application

We are not going to specify a format for applications.  It’s up to you whether you want to submit a word document, slides, video - whatever you think works best.

What we want to see is an outline of how ideas are proposed, debated and decided on and why you have selected the mechanisms you have. 

As mentioned we know this is the first stage of the application process - so don’t go overboard! It is not the most extensive or flashy applications that will get through but those that show they understand the challenges and potential solutions of governance.

Please also attach any other background/experience/CV that you may feel we should take into account when reviewing your application - whilst there is no specific background required for this role, it is a senior position so this will help us understand what experience you can draw upon and also where you might need more support from the wider team.

Following the application stage, there will be a short video call with our Talent Manager and a final interview with the relevant members of the Radix Leadership Team.
If you have issues uploading any of the above, please apply directly to farrah@rdx.works.
